newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 29.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Directors of munitions companies and Omnipol a.s., which were supposed to take part in exporting 100 tanks to Algeria pointed to the unclear conditions for exporting weapons. They said the cabinet caused domestic industry serious economic losses by rejecting this transaction.

- IPB bank had half-year net profits of 445.4 million crowns, according to Czech accounting standards, which is about 50 percent less than in the same period last year. Zivnostenska Banka's preliminary profits are 166.4 million crowns, which is only 62 percent of half-year profits last year.
- According to the bankruptcy administrator of Poldi Steel, Jan Ruzek, the situation in Poldi with bankrupt subsidiaries could bury hopes of renewing production.
- The financial division of South Korea's Samsung is interested in taking over Agrobanka, which has been under forced administration since last September.

- In the first half of this year, there were twice as many cases of drug crimes than in the first half of last year, according to the National Anti-Drug Centre. MLADA FRONTA DNES - The largest domestic lock maker, FAB, was taken over by Sweden's Assa Abloy, which now holds a 54-percent stake, according to the Securities Centre (SCP).
- Ostrava's Union Group, which owns Union Banka, became the dominant owner of another small domestic bank -- Foresbank. For now, Foresbank will remain an independent bank.
- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka announced yesterday a decrease in its prime rate by 0.45 percentage points and its base rates for credits of up to two years by 0.5 percentage points.
- The Finance Ministry announced yesterday that it will request that the Securities Centre introduce charges of one percent for transfers that take place over the counter.
- The new owner of Eska Cheb, Karlovy Vary businessman Radek Zahejsky, wants to obtain a foreign investor for the company which would provide necessary capital and end the company's long-term losses.
- Banka Hana decreased its reference rate yesterday by one percentage point to 17 percent.
PRAVO - The Czech Statistical Bureau decreased its original estimate for this year's grain harvest. The basic grain harvest should amount to 7,017 million tonnes, 8.6 percent more than last year.
- The leading world insurer Munich Re estimated flood damages in central Europe at 10 billion marks.
- Today, President Vaclav Havel will visit areas affected by the floods.
- Investicni a Postovni Banka signed to take on 250 million crowns worth of flood bonds, the largest amount so far from a mediating bank.
- So far, about 12 people from the Czech Republic have made enquiries about the possibility of recovering funds from Swiss banks lost after World War Two. Two to three Czechs enquire every day.
LIDOVE NOVINY - According to a survey from STEM, 19 percent of citizens were satisfied with the cabinet's work in July, while 81 percent were not satisfied.
- While 61 percent of Czechs said the economy was good and very good in an IVVM survey in February, in July this sum was only 38 percent.
